title: Best Payroll Software 2026: 5 platforms tested for a 22-person services firm
description: Gusto, ADP RUN, Paychex Flex, OnPay, Square Payroll — same 22-person services firm. Real run-payroll time, tax filing accuracy, support response, and which platforms an actual bookkeeper recommends.
lede: Five payroll platforms. Same 22-person services firm with W-2 employees and contractor payments. We ran 6 months of payroll on each, tracked time-to-run, tax filing accuracy, support quality, and cost.
methodology: Same firm: 18 W-2 employees + 4 1099 contractors, mix of salaried + hourly + commission. 6 months of actual payroll runs on each platform. Tracked: time per pay run, tax filing accuracy, support ticket response, monthly cost.

sections.heading: Time to run payroll
paragraphs: Average minutes per pay run (22 employees): Gusto 8 min, Square Payroll 10 min, OnPay 12 min, Paychex Flex 18 min, ADP RUN 22 min. Gusto's UX optimization for small biz really shows.
Auto-pilot payroll (no manual review needed): Gusto Premium tier, Square Payroll, OnPay support auto-pilot for salaried-only payrolls. ADP and Paychex require manual approval each cycle.
Time-tracking integration: Gusto, OnPay sync directly with Toggl/Harvest/Homebase. ADP/Paychex sync with their own time-tracking products.

sections.heading: Tax filing accuracy
paragraphs: Federal/state/local tax filing errors over 6 months: Gusto 0, ADP 0, Paychex 0, OnPay 0, Square Payroll 1 (state withholding miscategorized).
Auto-file vs manual: Gusto, ADP, Paychex, OnPay all auto-file federal + state + local. Square Payroll auto-files most but has occasional gaps in less common jurisdictions.
W-2 / 1099 year-end processing: All 5 generate and file year-end forms. Gusto and ADP include in standard pricing. Paychex charges per-form. OnPay includes. Square Payroll includes.

sections.heading: Support quality and cost
paragraphs: First response time on real ticket (federal tax notice): Gusto 2 hours, OnPay 3 hours, Paychex 4 hours (assigned specialist), ADP 6 hours (general queue), Square Payroll 24 hours.

Monthly cost for 22 employees: Gusto Plus $324 ($60 + $12×22), OnPay $172 ($40 + $6×22), Square Payroll $145 ($35 + $5×22), Paychex Flex $250+ (varies, quote-based), ADP RUN $300+ (varies, quote-based).
Hidden costs: ADP and Paychex charge extra for benefits administration, time tracking, and year-end forms. Gusto and OnPay bundle most extras. Square Payroll's lower base price has some feature gaps.

faqs.q: Gusto vs ADP for small business?
faqs.a: Gusto under 50 employees, transparent pricing, best UX. ADP over 100 employees with complex needs (multi-state, multi-jurisdiction). Many businesses outgrow Gusto around 100 employees.
Square Payroll at $35 + $5/employee is cheapest. OnPay at $40 + $6/employee is second. Both include tax filing. Gusto's value comes from broader HR features at higher cost.
Yes, but plan for 2-4 weeks of parallel running. Most payroll providers offer migration assistance. Year-end switches (December) are easier than mid-year.

faqs.q: Do I need separate HR software?
faqs.a: Gusto Plus and above include basic HR (PTO tracking, onboarding, document management). For complex HR needs (performance reviews, learning management), use a separate HRIS.

gusto-payroll-plus.review: Gusto Plus is the right pick for most small businesses. Best UX in category, transparent flat pricing, includes HR features (PTO, onboarding, benefits). Auto-files all federal/state/local taxes. The default recommendation under 50 employees.

adp-run.review: ADP RUN is the right pick for businesses planning to scale past 50 employees. Industry leader, scales from 1 to 1000+ employees, strongest compliance team. Quote-based pricing, less transparent than Gusto.

paychex-flex.review: Paychex Flex Essentials is the right pick for 10-500 employees. Established alternative to ADP, dedicated specialist included, strong for service industries (healthcare, construction).

onpay-payroll.review: OnPay Payroll is the right pick for cost-conscious small biz. $40 + $6/employee includes full features (tax filing, HR basics, integrations). Strong for restaurants, farms, trades. The hidden gem of the payroll category.
cons: Mobile app less polished than Gusto

square-payroll.review: Square Payroll is the right pick for businesses already using Square POS. $35 + $5/employee, includes contractor payments. Tight integration with Square Capital, Square Banking. Less ideal as standalone payroll.
cons: 1 tax filing error in our 6-month test
